title: Denton 1031 Exchange Coordination
name: Denton 1031 Exchange Coordination
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Denton student housing, Rayzor Ranch retail, and I-35E industrial growth, coordinated to the 45-day and 180-day deadlines.

sections.html: Denton sits at the northern edge of the metro, and its commercial base carries a distinct university influence that most other Dallas-area suburbs do not share. The University of North Texas and Texas Woman's University both support significant student-driven multifamily demand, Rayzor Ranch has built out a newer retail corridor serving the city's broader growth, and industrial and logistics buildings along the I-35E corridor have added supply as distribution activity pushes further north. The historic downtown square rounds out the picture with adaptive-reuse retail and restaurant space around the county courthouse. An exchanger sourcing Denton replacement property should expect to underwrite around an academic calendar in a way that most other suburbs in this metro simply do not require, and should expect fewer directly comparable sales to draw on than in a more established, non-university suburb closer to the metro core.

sections.heading: Student Housing Serving Two Universities
sections.html: Denton is unusual in the metro for supporting two separate university-driven housing markets, the University of North Texas and Texas Woman's University, and a property's pre-leasing pattern depends heavily on which campus it primarily serves, since the two schools do not share an identical academic calendar or student profile. A buyer should confirm which university a given multifamily property draws from before comparing its pre-leasing pace to a generic student-housing benchmark, since applying the wrong school's calendar assumptions to a property can make otherwise normal seasonal softness look like a leasing problem.

sections.heading: Rayzor Ranch Retail Corridor
sections.html: Rayzor Ranch has developed into Denton's primary newer retail corridor, with big-box and grocery-anchored centers serving both the university population and the city's broader residential growth, and this product generally carries more conventional retail underwriting than the historic downtown stock. A buyer should still confirm co-tenancy terms and current center occupancy before identification, since a corridor built to serve a growing but not yet fully mature trade area can carry more vacancy risk than the anchor tenant's own strength suggests. Smaller shop-space tenants along this corridor also tend to turn over more often than the anchors, so reviewing the full rent roll rather than just the anchor lease terms gives a more accurate picture of how the center actually performs day to day.

sections.heading: I-35E Industrial and Logistics Growth
sections.html:
Industrial and logistics building activity along the I-35E corridor has picked up as distribution tenants look further north for sites, and several of these buildings are new enough that they carry limited trailing operating history compared with an established industrial submarket closer to the metro core. A diligence file for I-35E replacement property typically includes:

  • Clear height and dock door count against current tenant requirements
  • Trailer parking and truck court capacity
  • Remaining lease term against tenant buildout cost
  • Utility capacity confirmation given the pace of nearby growth
  • Phase I environmental site assessment
  • Tenant estoppel certificates

Confirming utility capacity is worth the extra step in this corridor, since infrastructure has not always kept pace with the rate of new industrial and residential construction pushing north along I-35E.

sections.heading: Identification Timing Around the Academic Calendar
sections.html: Because student housing demand in Denton concentrates its leasing activity in a narrow spring window ahead of the fall semester, exchangers considering a university-driven multifamily candidate should time their diligence and lender submission to avoid getting caught mid-review during that pre-leasing period, and often name a Rayzor Ranch or I-35E industrial candidate alongside it under the three-property rule so a slower-moving academic-calendar deal does not consume the entire 45-day identification window on its own.

sections.heading: Qualified Intermediary and Lender Coordination for University-Adjacent Assets
sections.html: Lenders financing Denton student housing typically request pre-leasing data specific to the relevant university's calendar rather than a generic multifamily benchmark, and providing that context up front tends to shorten underwriting relative to treating the deal like a conventional apartment acquisition. The qualified intermediary holds exchange proceeds throughout this process and releases them at closing; this describes process and coordination only, and Denton exchangers should confirm tax treatment with their own advisor before the 180-day deadline arrives.

faqs.q: Does it matter which university a Denton student housing property serves?
faqs.a: Yes. The University of North Texas and Texas Woman's University do not share an identical academic calendar or student profile, so confirm which school a property draws from before comparing its pre-leasing pace to a generic benchmark.

faqs.q: Is Rayzor Ranch retail as stabilized as an established Dallas-area retail corridor?
faqs.a: Generally yes for underwriting purposes, but confirm co-tenancy terms and current center occupancy, since a still-maturing trade area can carry more vacancy risk than the anchor tenant's strength alone suggests.

faqs.q: What should I confirm before identifying an I-35E industrial building in Denton?
faqs.a: Confirm utility capacity in addition to the usual clear height and dock door review, since infrastructure has not always kept pace with the rate of new construction along this corridor.

faqs.q: Why would I pair a student housing candidate with an industrial building in the same exchange?
faqs.a: The academic calendar can slow diligence and lender review on a university-driven property, so naming a Rayzor Ranch or I-35E candidate alongside it under the three-property rule keeps the 45-day window from being consumed by one slower-moving deal.

faqs.q: Do lenders need different information for Denton student housing than a typical apartment deal?
faqs.a: Often, yes, requesting pre-leasing data specific to the relevant university's calendar. The qualified intermediary still holds and directs exchange funds; this is process description only, and investors should confirm tax treatment with their own advisor.
